newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK OAE TO CLOSE DOWN IN THREE YEARS-INDUSTRY MIN.
newsitem.headline: GREEK OAE TO CLOSE DOWN IN THREE YEARS-INDUSTRY MIN.

text.p: The Reconstruction Organisation of Ailing Enterprises (OAE) will take three years to close down as potential buyers are reluctant to invest in loss-making firms, Development Minister Vasso Papanfreou said on Tuesday.

"We want OAE to close down as soon as possible but the process is time-consuming. It's not enough to sell. You also need a buyer. I would say it will take about three years," Papandreou told an American-Hellenic Chamber of Commerce conference on the Greek Economy.
She also said long court cases over the clearance of the firms hindered their selling.
National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou told the same conference on Sunday that OAE would close down within next year.
OAE was formed in 1983, grouping under the state's ombrella ailing private firms which were about to close down. Some 13 companies remain to be cleared or sold.
Ministry officials said Athens Paper Mills, Elefsis Boxites, Kerafina and MEL were four OAE firms which would probably be sold next year.
Asked to comment on the country's foreign exchange policy, Papandreou said the depreciation of the drachma could not be used any longer as a tool to improve long-term competitiveness.

"The sliding of the drachma can't be used any longer to boost competitiviness. It is an effective measure in the short-term but it creates problems, like inflation, in the long term," she said. --Costas Paris, Intercontinental Newsroom, 30-1-9226961
